title: Understanding the Loss Function
text: Let's start by examining the loss function \( \tilde{L}(\theta) $$=$$ 2\theta_0 + \theta_0**4\theta_1 - e**{2\theta_1} \). Notice how each term involves \( $$\theta_0$$ \) and \( $$\theta_1$$ \). Consider how each term will contribute to the gradient with respect to \( $$\theta_0$$ \).

title: Partial Derivative with Respect to \( $$\theta_0$$ \)
text: To find the gradient descent update for \( $$\theta_0$$ \), we need the partial derivative of \( \tilde{L} \) with respect to \( $$\theta_0$$ \). Focus on the terms in \( \tilde{L} \) that include \( $$\theta_0$$ \). What happens when you differentiate \( 2\theta_0 \) and \( \theta_0**4\theta_1 \) with respect to \( $$\theta_0$$ \)?

title: Gradient Descent Update Formula
text: Remember, the update rule for gradient descent is \( \theta_0**{(1)} $$=$$ \theta_0**{(0)} - \alpha \cdot \frac{\partial \tilde{L}}{\partial $$\theta_0$$} \). You have \( \theta_0**{(0)} $$=$$ $$1$$ \) and \( \alpha $$=$$ $$0.5$$ \). Use these values to calculate the update.

title: Calculate the Partial Derivative
text: What is the partial derivative of \( \tilde{L} \) with respect to \( $$\theta_0$$ \) when \( $$\theta_0$$ $$=$$ $$1$$ \) and \( $$\theta_1$$ $$=$$ $$2$$ \)?

title: Apply the Gradient Descent Update
text: Using the partial derivative you calculated, what is the new value of \( \theta_0**{(1)} \) after applying the gradient descent update?
